title: Cortex-FL: Agent-Mediated Collaboration for Federated Learning
summary: Federated learning (FL) enables independent data owners to train models collaboratively without centralizing raw data. However, identifying collaborators, preparing training tasks, and coordinating execution and incentives hinder its practical adoption by organizations without specialized expertise. We present Cortex-FL, an agent-native FL system that enables users to express learning objectives in natural language and delegate the collaboration required to train a model. Agents translate these objectives into shared tasks, discover collaborators, and negotiate participation agreements, connecting collaboration formation with distributed training and incentive management. The architecture separates agent coordination from local execution authority, allowing owners to delegate coordination while retaining control over their data, computation, and financial commitments. We demonstrate the complete workflow on a four-node deployment, in which a model requested in natural language proceeds through collaboration formation, contract-governed training, verified model delivery, and x402 settlement on a blockchain testnet.

title: From Delegation to Coordination: Learning Efficient Multi-Agent Deep Research
summary: Multi-agent deep-research systems use delegation to parallelize search and keep long tool traces out of the main agent's context. Yet delegation helps only when task allocation and subtask execution are coordinated: the main agent must issue useful subtasks, while subagents must return reliable evidence. Existing training either optimizes only the main agent or broadcasts the same team advantage to all agents, which can reward misleading subagent reports and penalize useful ones. We introduce LEAD-RL (Learning Effective Agent Delegation with Reinforcement Learning), a joint main-agent-subagent training framework with contribution-aware credit assignment. A training-time rubric evaluates the research utility of each subagent report and gates its inherited team advantage, while final-answer correctness remains the only team reward; no token, step, or speedup reward is used. Across five benchmarks and two model families, LEAD-RL improves answer quality. On BrowseComp, it improves accuracy by 2.49 percentage points and reduces critical-path cost by 24.5% over joint training with shared team credit. During validation, accuracy increases by 6.78 points at approximately constant critical-path cost. These results show that contribution-aware credit assignment improves the quality-efficiency trade-off of multi-agent deep research.

title: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents
summary: Autonomous agents modify prompts, memories, tools, workflows, and policies using interaction histories. Yet a plausible modification is not necessarily suitable for persistent adoption: candidate selection is adaptive, evaluators may be imperfect, and local gains can hide degradation against an earlier baseline. We introduce Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework for governing adoption of self-generated agent modifications. EGE separates candidate generation from confirmatory adoption, evaluates frozen candidates on fresh paired audits, requires meaningful improvement on a prespecified primary objective, protects declared capabilities through reference-relative non-inferiority tests, and applies governance constraints before bounded canary deployment. We establish an evaluator-calibrated simultaneous lower-bound construction for a countable sequence of adaptively generated candidates. It combines candidate-wise Hoeffding bounds with independent calibration samples comparing the operational evaluator with a prespecified reference procedure. We also formalise reference replacement through bridge tests, derive a cumulative degradation bound along a versioned reference lineage, and provide an audit-planning condition relating effect-size margin, sample sizes, and acceptance probability. A Monte Carlo stress test illustrates calibration under candidate-dependent evaluator optimism; it is a stylised statistical experiment, not an evaluation of a deployed agent. The guarantees are conditional on bounded paired scores, fresh sampling, a valid reference-evaluation construct, and declared evaluation distributions; they do not establish universal agent safety or robustness to arbitrary distribution shift.

title: Shared Item-Level Error Limits the Aggregation of Small Language Models in Fermi Estimation
summary: Multi-agent systems of language models are often motivated by an averaging argument: if the agents' errors are unbiased and independent, the error of an aggregate of N answers falls as 1/sqrt(N). Fermi estimation, whose continuous answers are aggregated on the logarithmic scale, permits a direct test. We decompose the log10 error of each answer into the mean error of its model on the item, common to all its draws on the item, and a residual, and estimate both from 2.51M answers given before any communication by 15 open-weight models (3B-72B) on realFP, with replication under a single prompt pair on realFP, Science Olympiad Fermi questions and a guesstimation set. Given the item, teammates' errors are uncorrelated and teams behave as independent draws, but the item-level component accounts for a median 0.906 of the error variance over items. Teams of thirty therefore reduce a single agent's error by a median 1.7% (at most 5.4%), whereas draws that were also unbiased on each item would reduce it by 74-79%. All models compress their estimates toward about 10^6; this trend explains a median 17% of the item-level component, and a cross-validated linear recalibration on labelled items removes the overall bias but not that component. Three rounds of debate reduce within-team dispersion by 93% and leave the item-level component unchanged; revision without peers attains the same small gain. Mixing five models of similar accuracy reduces error by 6.6% relative to their own homogeneous teams, but no mixture improves on the most accurate model. Higher sampling temperature changes team error by about 1% at most, and contrastive activation steering not detectably; per-agent scaffold prompts (not significant after multiplicity correction) and skipping one layer in a single-model screen improve it. The results are conditional on the models, benchmarks, prompts and settings tested.

title: SwarmSafe-Delta: Isolating Message Effects on LLM Agent Safety
summary:
When a tool-using LLM agent team violates policy, aggregate outcomes do not reveal whether an upstream message changed the executor's action. We introduce SwarmSafe-Delta, a paired executable protocol that freezes upstream computation, varies real, hidden, and format-matched placebo delivery, and scores a single committed action against deterministic benign and risky policy states under preassigned budgets.
Across four models and constructed optional tasks, real delivery at $N=4$ produces 21.4% risky-world violations, versus 5.0% with placebo and 1.0% with hidden delivery (paired differences +16.4 and +20.3 percentage points). Real delivery also improves benign task success, illustrating that suppressing communication sacrifices utility. In a second regime constructed to require an upstream lookup route, real delivery improves safe completion by 74.2 points relative to hidden delivery. These effects quantify message-delivery contrasts under specified information dependencies, not naturally occurring failure rates.
Exploratory action-level analyses show that the effect depends strongly on whether the upstream message recommends a prerequisite check or direct execution; model differences also largely track these message compositions. The contribution is a controlled, execution-grounded measurement protocol rather than a general claim that agent communication is harmful or protective.

title: Gradient-Aware AI Agents for Autonomous Turbulence Model Discovery via Differentiable CFD
summary: Turbulence modeling relies on human choices of closure form, physical inputs, and tunable parameters. Training closures a posteriori is efficient only with gradients through long chaotic rollouts, which few solvers provide. Most a posteriori approaches therefore resort to gradient-free optimization, and nearly all fix the closure form in advance, learning only its parameters. In this work, we introduce a gradient-aware agentic framework that poses closure discovery as a bilevel problem: a multi-agent large language model (LLM) system searches over closure forms, while a GPU-native differentiable computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solver supplies gradients, making differentiable a posteriori learning an action of the autonomous AI agent. For each proposal, the agents construct a differentiable training program by embedding the analytical, neural, or hybrid closure in the solver, implementing a differentiable objective, and validating the gradient path. They then decide whether to evaluate the closure, compute its parameter sensitivities, or train it a posteriori, select the optimization settings, and revise subsequent proposals using the simulation outcomes and returned gradients. Truncated-horizon gradients make this training usable under chaotic dynamics for closures with tens of thousands of parameters. Demonstrations include dissipation-law and subgrid-scale closure discovery in two-dimensional turbulence and wall-model discovery for large-eddy simulation of three-dimensional channel flow. With gradient-based training, the agent recovers reference coefficients that forward evaluation alone does not reach within the same budget, and autonomously discovers and trains analytical and neural closures that improve agreement with the targeted reference statistics. These results demonstrate the feasibility of end-to-end autonomous turbulence model development in time-resolved flows.

title: Food Critic: An Agentic Visualization System for Auditable Restaurant-Safety Reasoning
summary: Generative AI agents are increasingly being embedded into visualization systems that can search data, invoke tools, summarize evidence, and produce recommendations. However, when agents rely solely on their own knowledge, the visualization problem is not only whether the agent provides a useful answer, but also whether users can inspect how that answer is grounded. We present Food Critic, an agentic visualization system for diners' restaurant decision support that integrates public health inspection records with crowd review data. The system grounds agents under three conditions: a database-only ReAct agent, a retrieval- augmented agent with access to food-safety regulations, and an ontology-guided agent that produces structured hypotheses and typed evidence. Food Critic externalizes the agent's reasoning within these groundings as inspectable visual evidence. We evaluate LLM models with several use cases under each grounding of our agentic system. Our work positions restaurant choice as a concrete case for studying human-agent collaboration, visual provenance of agent reasoning, and the design of visual interfaces for grounded GenAI decision support.

title: Before AI Agents Negotiate for Us: A Competitive Tournament of Rule-Based, Search, Optimization, Learned, and Language-Model Negotiators Under Scarcity
summary: Automated bilateral negotiation underlies two-sided matching markets such as freight brokering, where many shippers and carriers negotiate price before a matching mechanism decides who is paired with whom. Prior strategy comparisons typically use isolated one-on-one duels or a single fixed market, so they cannot show how a strategy behaves against several live rivals under a changing balance of supply and demand. We built nine negotiation architectures spanning rule-based, search-based, optimization-based, imitation-learning, and reinforcement-learning families, and ran all nine simultaneously on both sides of a Gale-Shapley matching market under a balanced condition and two scarcity conditions rotated across all 36 exclusion pairs. In the balanced carrier market, an imitation-learned engine (ML2), a reinforcement-learning policy trained only on isolated negotiations (RL), and an expected-utility optimization engine (OPT) formed a statistically tied top group, and no architecture led in every condition and role. RL beat all eight carrier rivals when carriers were scarce, but its match rate collapsed from 62% to 16% when shippers were scarce and it had to compete with the other carrier agents for demand. A second reinforcement-learning policy trained against rival agents (RL2) kept its match rate above 91% in every condition, yet lost on realized payoff to all eight shipper-side rivals in two of the three conditions, traced to a confirmed train/deployment feature mismatch. We also tested nine large language models (LLMs), from 1 to 72 billion parameters, under the same protocol: they lost significantly to the two strongest engines (OPT2 and ML2) in 32 of 36 comparisons and won none. These results show that isolated or single-condition evaluation can hide failure modes that a many-sided, scarcity-varying, statistically corrected tournament exposes directly.

title: MULTILOOP: Evolving Multi-Agent Harnesses for Complex Information-Seeking Tasks
summary: The performance of LLM-based agents depends not only on the underlying model but also on the harness: the prompts, tools, and orchestration logic around it. Recent works automate harness optimization with coding agents that analyze execution traces, diagnose failures, and edit the harness code; however, those focused on single-agent systems. Multi-agent harnesses are harder to optimize as fixing them requires changing how agents interact in addition to how each behaves. We study whether automated harness optimization can diagnose and repair failures in multi-agent systems through a case study on complex information-seeking tasks from DeepSearchQA [Gupta et al., 2026]. We apply MULTILOOP, a simple optimization loop in which a coding agent iteratively analyzes, evaluates and edits the harness. With only 10 training samples, the evolved harness improves accuracy by 4.6% over the base harness and by 3.2% over the best single-agent system. However, a taxonomy of failure modes before and after optimization shows that the orchestration failures that characterize multi-agent systems largely persist. Our findings motivate harness optimization methods that encourage structural changes to how agents delegate tasks and share information.

With only 10 training samples, the evolved harness improves accuracy by 4.6% over the base harness and by 3.2% over the best single-agent system. However, a taxonomy of failure modes before and after optimization shows that the orchestration failures that characterize multi-agent systems largely persist. Our findings motivate harness optimization methods that encourage structural changes to how agents delegate tasks and share information.

title: DecArena: Evaluating Large-Scale Decentralized Multi-Agent Collaboration
summary: Emerging personal AI agents raise fundamental scalability and privacy concerns for centralized multi-agent systems (MASs), which rely on a global orchestrator with broad access to agents, resources, and communication. In decentralized environments, global visibility is unavailable. Agents need to proactively discover non-local resources (e.g. tools, skills), and collaborate with other agents to solve tasks. We study decentralized multi-agent collaboration under graph-constrained communication, a natural reflection of human structures. Each agent observes only its local state and can interact only with neighboring agents. We introduce a benchmark with synthetic scalable distributed tool calling with 100K+ tools. Our experiments reveal that recent LLM agents struggle to discover non-local relevant resources and collaborate in decentralized setting. Moreover, standard reinforcement learning fails to reliably overcome this limitation, suggesting that decentralized MAS needs more explicit harness mechanisms for effective collaboration, even using SOTA LLMs. We then present a strong baseline \textbf{GraphHarness}, combining topology-aware warmup with self-improving LLM-based routing. Results show that GraphHarness substantially improves task success (+48.5) and produces higher quality collaboration (+30.6), while using fewer costs (+34.0) than baselines.

title: BrickFlow: Connectivity-Guided Brick Reconstruction
summary: Given a set of LEGO parts and an image of an assembled object, our task is to infer the pose of each part to assemble the object. In contrast with traditional 3D reconstruction, doing so requires satisfying discrete physical constraints, which provide structure but render the problem combinatorial and highly sensitive to small pose errors. To learn a prior over how parts fit together, we train a set-conditioned SE(3) flow model on procedurally generated assemblies. We then finetune this model to inject image conditioning, using 1% as much data. However, while the learned flow captures global structure, it does not enforce connectivity. To address this, we introduce an analytic connectivity-field guidance to pull predictions toward connected assemblies at test time. Through this, we demonstrate improved build quality with model size, pretraining, and guidance. We make our models and data available for research purposes at https://kulits.github.io/BrickFlow/

title: Consistent Video-to-Video Translation via Explicit Correspondences
summary: Interactive video-to-video applications require real-time generation while maintaining long-range temporal consistency. However, recent methods achieve speed by restricting attention to a fixed-length causal window. This limits long-range consistency whenever relevant history falls outside the context window. To address this limitation, we introduce vid2vid-long, a correspondence-based approach grounded in a simple observation. Video-to-video translation provides an explicit cross-frame reference: the regions that match in the input video should match in the output video too. Concretely, we compute patch-level correspondences in the input, guiding retrieval of previously generated outputs in the corresponding regions, and condition the model on these patches through correspondence cross-attention. Our experiments demonstrate that vid2vid-long consistently improves long-range temporal consistency across recent video models while preserving generation quality and real-time performance.

title: Neural Render Proxies for Interactive and Differentiable Lighting
summary: Within the CG animation production pipeline, the challenges artists tackle in Lighting can be immense. Even minor adjustments require re-rendering massive scenes with slow offline renderers; global illumination has to be sampled and complex shaders have to be evaluated, leading to iteration times of minutes to hours per frame. To accelerate this process, we introduce a novel neural render proxy (NRP) that enables differentiable relighting of static scenes with fixed camera and materials at interactive rates. Our main insight is the decoupling of traditional rendering into path sampling and emission computation. From a single, light-agnostic render pass, we collect light transport data in the form of path samples. This enables rapidly sampling lighting conditions on the fly, and training a scene-specific lightweight neural network that learns how light is transported from any scene location to any image pixel. This approach is compatible with non-differentiable production renderers, induces minimal memory requirements during inference, and scales only with resolution and the number of light sources and parameters, but independently of scene and appearance complexity. Our evaluation demonstrates interactive frame rates for relighting (~30-60 Hz) while closely approximating the visual fidelity of ground-truth path tracing. In addition, the differentiable NRP enables fast, gradient-based inverse workflows, allowing artists to efficiently solve for lighting parameters from intuitive image-space edits or generative targets.

title: Sprint3D: Accelerating End-to-End 3D Asset Generation through Pipeline Optimization
summary: Image-to-3D generative models now produce asset-quality textured meshes, but at minutes per asset they remain slow to iterate with and costly to deploy. Prior work has mostly accelerated the sampling of the networks, and where it also optimizes the mesh processing, it trains its own generators. We instead start from a publicly released pipeline and ask how much of its end-to-end time can be saved. Profiling the public Pixal3D pipeline shows that its latency is dominated by what happens after the networks: the four rectified flows take 14% of the wall-clock time and mesh post-processing takes 85%, most of it in CPU-based UV unwrapping. We therefore first rebuild the mesh post-processing on the GPU and take it off the critical path, then cut the per-evaluation overhead of the flows and distill them from 76 to 8 network evaluations. The resulting pipeline, Sprint3D, reduces the median time per asset from 133 s to 4.05 s on one H200 GPU at the same export settings (33$\times$). At the same time, on 2,653 held-out Toys4K objects it improves every input-view normal metric of the Pixal3D protocol, with a slightly lower mean silhouette IoU, lower point-cloud alignment scores and less fine texture detail. The rebuilt post-processing alone also speeds up TRELLIS.2, which uses the same export code, by 6.7$\times$ without a detectable change in the evaluated metrics.

title: PIM: A Physical Intuition Model for Low-Latency Prediction of Object Interaction Outcomes
summary: Predicting object interaction outcomes from initial conditions is a central problem in data-driven physical reasoning. Existing methods often use rigid-body-level states or predict the evolution through autoregressive rollouts. Coarse representations cannot represent local deformation, while rollout errors may compound over long prediction horizons. Instead, we introduce PIM, a Physical Intuition Model that directly predicts a physical system's equilibrium state from its initial mesh geometry, kinematics, and physical attributes. PIM combines local k-nearest-neighbor (KNN) attention to encode intra-object geometry, anchor-based cross-object attention to model interactions, and a dual-branch decoder that predicts object-level translations and per-vertex residual displacements. Across MuJoCo scenarios involving both rigid and deformable interactions, PIM achieves lower vertex and centroid errors than the evaluated baselines. By predicting complete equilibrium states in a single forward pass, PIM substantially reduces latency relative to autoregressive learned models and MuJoCo rollouts under the evaluated protocols, enabling low-latency inference when only the final outcome is required.

title: Delaunay-Based Nearest Neighbor Search with Grid-Accelerated Queries and Parallel Construction
summary: Nearest-neighbor search is a fundamental primitive in computer graphics, with applications in distance field computation, surface reconstruction, and point cloud registration. In many graphics applications, data points lie on a surface manifold embedded in 3D space, whereas queries are distributed throughout the surrounding volume, a setting in which spatial partitioning structures such as k-d trees and grids can become inefficient. Dynamic-programming-based nearest-neighbor search (DP-NNS) offers an alternative: it traverses a successor DAG that records the history of incremental Delaunay construction and often outperforms spatial partitioning structures. However, its sequential construction is slow, and naive parallelization degrades query performance, limiting its practical adoption. We accelerate both queries and construction in DP-NNS. For queries, we introduce a grid-based initialization strategy that precomputes valid starting points on the successor DAG, shortening search paths while preserving exactness and enabling a twofold speedup. For construction, we analyze how parallel insertion affects query cost and develop a parallel algorithm that preserves logarithmic expected query cost under stated geometric assumptions. Our parallel construction algorithm achieves a 10x speedup over the sequential baseline while maintaining nearly the same query cost. We further reorder query points to improve cache locality. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms widely used libraries in nearest-neighbor query performance.

title: A Lightweight Differentiable Method for Real-Time Skin Rendering and Digitization
summary: Inverse rendering for skin typically relies on offline path tracing to estimate physical properties, which fail to map directly to the approximate shaders utilized in interactive applications, such as game engines. We bridge this gap by directly estimating subsurface scattering parameters tailored for real-time rendering pipelines. We introduce a differentiable Screen-Space Subsurface Scattering (SSSS) framework that enables the joint optimization of spatially varying base textures and scattering distances. To account for local variations in skin thickness, we estimate these parameters across distinct facial regions, generating a blended profile map ready for production runtime engines. Our pipeline utilizes a low-cost, single-light, single-view capture setup designed for accessible and practical appearance acquisition. Optimization is driven by a masked loss function targeting regions where subsurface scattering effects are dominant. We validate our approach on a real-world dataset of $45$ individuals across the Monk Skin Tone Scale, ensuring demographic generalization. Furthermore, we complement this evaluation with synthetic data, a multi-light setup validating our single-light assumption, and a tilted-view configuration confirming angular consistency. Results demonstrate that our method effectively recovers scattering parameters from lightweight inputs, yielding realistic skin appearance directly compatible with standard real-time shaders.

title: Linear-size graphs at every strict dismantling level
summary: Dismantling reduces a graph to one vertex by successive deletions. At level zero, a vertex is eligible if one of its neighbours is adjacent to all its other neighbours. At level $k\geq1$, its neighbours must induce a graph dismantlable at level $k-1$. A graph has strict level $k$ if it admits a reduction at level $k$ and none at level $k-1$. For every $k\geq1$, we construct a graph of strict level $k$ with $3k+8$ vertices. Each step adds three vertices: the neighbours of one induce the preceding graph, and the other two provide the adjacencies used to rule out other first deletions at the lower level. A second construction gives a graph of order $4k+4$ at strict level $k$. Together the two families give the upper bound $\min\{4k+4,3k+8\}$ on the least order at strict level $k$.

title: FAME-QP: A GPU-Accelerated Quadratic-Programming Solver for Real-Time Model Predictive Control
summary: We present FAME-QP, a GPU-accelerated solver for dense quadratic programs arising in linear model predictive control. FAME-QP combines constraint-dependent operator representations with fused single- and two-kernel iterations replayed through CUDA graphs, automatically selecting the execution configuration through device calibration and problem-specific timing. It probes a cached operator bank to select the initial penalty and updates operators lazily when problem matrices change. Numerical benchmarks and simulated humanoid and quadrotor control experiments demonstrate reduced latency relative to competing GPU solvers while maintaining solution accuracy and control performance.

title: Deformable Texture Maps: Compiling Dynamic Microgeometry into Neural Textures
summary: Deformable material surfaces, such as cloth, owe their appearance to fine-scale geometries that restructure under deformation. Even when coarse simulation models efficiently recover this microstructure, explicitly instantiating and rendering it remains expensive. We introduce Deformable Texture Maps (DTM), a representation that compiles deformation-driven microgeometry into a continuous and compact neural texture. Our model maps texture coordinates and local deformations to intrinsic maps describing opacity, surface normals, depth, and material identity. This captures the occlusion and visibility changes generated by deformation. At runtime, these maps provide a common texture-space representation of deformation-driven fine-scale structure that can be evaluated directly on coarse deforming surfaces. Since our representation encodes geometric attributes rather than radiance, lighting and material response remain decoupled from the learned model. This allows us to apply relighting, as well as shading and material editing without retraining. We further introduce a persistent texture-space rendering strategy that caches these intrinsic maps and selectively updates them as deformation changes. This effectively decouples neural evaluation from frame rendering and enables their reuse across frames and conventional rendering effects. We demonstrate our approach on yarn-based textiles, where non-linear material stretch and shear induce changes in yarn geometry, spacing and occlusion. We build our model by, first, sweeping tileable yarn patches through deformation space, then, rendering the detailed geometry into a canonical texture-space, and finally, compressing the resulting maps into a single neural representation. Our resulting model can be evaluated directly on arbitrary coarse garment meshes and integrated with conventional shading pipelines, keeping appearance authorable at render time.

title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
summary: Light can manipulate magnetic order and its excitations on ultrafast timescales, including through resonantly driven phonons. In antiferromagnets, light can also create correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons. Unlike single magnons, whose damping has been measured and modeled in detail, little is known about the lifetime, interactions and decay of such correlated pairs: prior two-magnon measurements show broad linewidths or coherences that dephase within 200 fs. Here we pump the phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption of NiO with mid-infrared pulses, far below its bandgap, and probe the resulting magnetic dynamics at finite momentum with time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS). Upon photoexcitation, the one-magnon linewidth and energy are essentially unchanged, indicating that the long-range magnetic order is preserved without the photocarrier-induced demagnetization characteristic of above-bandgap excitation. A pump-induced two-magnon signal appears on the energy-gain (anti-Stokes) side of the spectrum. Its spectral weight peaks 4 ps after the pump, well beyond our 0.5 ps time resolution, indicative of a delayed growth likely due to momentum redistribution of the light-induced magnon pairs across the Brillouin zone. This two-magnon signal decays with a time constant of $28\pm11$ ps, exceeding the previously reported two-magnon dephasing time by more than two orders of magnitude. These results establish long-lived light-driven bimagnon correlations beyond the one-magnon state, akin to the higher-order correlations measured in ultracold gases.

title: SiC-BN composites with extreme thermal and environmental stability
summary: Ceramic materials that maintain structural integrity and resist thermal-shock under extreme conditions are critical for many applications. Here we show that spark plasma sintered composites containing equal weight fractions of hexagonal silicon carbide (6H-SiC) and boron nitride (h-BN) exhibit exceptional stability under extreme high-temperature oxidizing conditions and unusually stable temperature-independent thermal conductivity across a broad temperature range. Under high-velocity oxygen-fuel torch exposure in air, it withstands prolonged heating and thermal-cycling at surface temperatures reaching >1500 °C, whereas pure 6H-SiC and h-BN rapidly fractures or erodes. Microstructural evaluation shows the formation of a multi-phase surface silica layer that further protects the material from oxidation. Finite-element analysis heat-flux map shows that intrinsic porosity mitigates thermal stress, while ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations reveal thermally driven interfacial reconstruction and the formation of a Si-N/C-B-rich bonding network, enhancing the interfacial cohesion at elevated temperatures. This lightweight, easily machinable ceramic composite will be a promising structural material in extreme environment applications.

title: Circular phonons generate negligible magnetization in insulators
summary: The optical excitation of circular phonons has opened up non-equilibrium phenomena with no equilibrium counterparts, ranging from the generation of synthetic magnetic fields to the control of topological order or the manipulation of ferroaxial states. In this area, significant controversy has arisen on whether sizeable "true" magnetizations accompany circular phonons. Several confounding factors cloud the interpretation of the experiments, which are based on probing polarization rotation in the driven material. These range from the interpretation of the Faraday effect in non-equilibrium conditions to spurious nonlinear optical contributions in pump probe experiments. Here we resolve these ambiguities by measuring both polarization rotation inside the driven material and the stray magnetic field generated outside it with a proximate Faraday detector. For a 5 MV/cm mid-infrared drive, we observe a colossal polarization rotation inside a driven SiC crystal, similar to what was reported in previous work. Depending on the assumptions made, this could correspond to magnetizations as high as $μ_0 M = 0.3 T$ or as low as 4 $μT$. However, when measuring the magnetic stray field outside the driven sample we unambiguously determine that the magnetization in SiC is negligibly small ($μ_0 M \lt 0.001 T$).

Depending on the assumptions made, this could correspond to magnetizations as high as $μ_0 M = 0.3 T$ or as low as 4 $μT$. However, when measuring the magnetic stray field outside the driven sample we unambiguously determine that the magnetization in SiC is negligibly small ($μ_0 M \lt 0.001 T$).

title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design
summary: Automatic differentiation has enabled rapid progress on continuous-variable mechanical design problems, but gradient-based optimization still struggles with discrete variables. The standard approach is to optimize using a continuous relaxation of the choices, then commit to the nearest discrete design at the end. Why this procedure selects unfavorable basins is poorly understood. Here, we introduce a practical, interpretable design problem inspired by origami, in which automatic differentiation is used to design shapes with a target functional behavior. Each origami sheet has a fixed geometry, and a bilevel optimization framework tunes which one of four discrete hinge types to place at each fold. Baseline gradient-based design settles into basins with a large discretization gap: relaxed optimization solves 97% of runs, but the final, discrete solutions succeed only half the time. We find that the gap can be relieved with a surprisingly simple modification. An initialization prior uniformly biased toward the stiff, flat hinge option boosts the final solve fraction from 49% to 69%. Applying the prior adds no additional compute and leaves the optimization process unchanged. Compared to the baseline, sheets produced with the prior have greater geometric compatibility and mechanical stiffness. Directly penalizing frustration and floppiness in the outer loss function produces an even greater improvement than the prior does, raising the solve fraction to 78% and indicating that these properties help distinguish the unfavorable basins. Our results demonstrate that loss landscapes for mechanical design can have physically meaningful basins that are not robust to discretization and cause solves to fail. Targeting these basins' physical signatures, even with just an initialization bias, helps avoid them.

title: High-pressure behavior of the low-frequency mode of water
summary: The low-frequency (LF) mode observed in the THz spectrum of liquid water near 10 meV has been known for decades, yet its microscopic origin remains debated. Leading interpretations assign it to a transverse acoustic-like excitation, a transverse optic-like mode, or a mode-mode coupling mechanism. We address this question by probing the collective dynamics of H$_2$O and D$_2$O at room temperature and pressures from 0.1 to 1 GPa using high-resolution (1.6 meV) inelastic X-ray scattering (IXS). The LF mode remains heavily damped, close to critical damping, throughout the explored range, while its frequency hardens markedly with pressure, much more than expected for a transverse acoustic mode. Comparison with IXS measurements and \textit{ab initio} simulations of crystalline Ice VI reveals a cluster of weakly dispersive modes in the same energy range, suggesting that the low-frequency mode in liquid water reflects a mixed character arising from the superposition of several branches rather than a single well-defined excitation, providing a coherent microscopic picture of water's anomalous THz dynamics under compression.

title: Two Unconventional Hall Effects in the Kagome Magnet TmMn4Cr$_2$Sn$_6$
summary: We identify two Hall anomalies in the kagome magnet TmMn$_4$Cr$_2$Sn$_6$. We propose that the high-field anomaly reflects a discontinuous spin reorientation and differing sublattice contributions to Hall transport and magnetization. At low fields, Hall hysteresis persists despite negligible magnetic hysteresis, suggesting a chirality-related contribution, although its microscopic origin remains unresolved. These contrasting regimes show how magnetic transitions can mimic unconventional Hall signals and highlight the limits of magnetization-based Hall decomposition.

title: Large Pockels Effect in Multiaxial Ferroelectrics Induced by Polarization Reorientation
summary: Materials with large linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect have significant potential for fabricating energy-efficient photonic devices. Previous strategies have mostly relied on structural softness---associated with phase boundary, domain wall, or strain induced phase transition---to create large Pockels effect in ferroelectrics. In this Letter, we show that polarization reorientation in multiaxial ferroelectrics may create structural softness and thus induce large Pockels effect. By developing a phenomenological theory, we find that multiaxial ferroelectrics exhibit a hysteretic relationship between the azimuth angles of the polarization and the electric field, and a possible divergence of the linear electro-optic coefficient may occur at an appropriate polarization azimuth angle. This suggests a brand-new strategy for engineering large Pockels effect in multiaxial ferroelectrics. We perform first-principles simulations on several multiaxial ferroelectrics and predict that polarization reorientation can significantly enhance the electro-optic coefficients in monolayer SnSe and bulk KNbO$_3$. This validates the soundness of our strategy and emphasizes multiaxial ferroelectrics as promising platforms toward large Pockels effect.

title: Tailored magnetic domain-wall ratchet effects through density gradients in triangular-hole arrays
summary: We investigate domain wall (DW) dynamics and morphology in amorphous Co$_{0.86}$Zr$_{0.14}$ thin films patterned with engineered, density-graded triangular-hole arrays. Using Kerr microscopy and high-resolution XMCD-PEEM imaging, we demonstrate that DW propagation is governed by the interplay between hole orientation, density gradients, and local magnetostatic interactions. In cooperative configurations, the density gradient reinforces the geometric ratchet effect, whereas in competing configurations, the two mechanisms oppose each other, leading to an inverse ratchet and enabling experimental access to backward DW propagation. Remarkably, density-graded arrays substantially reduce the stochastic variability of depinning fields observed in periodic arrays, resulting in highly reproducible DW motion. The depinning fields are described by a rigid DW model and an empirical scaling law incorporating both inter-hole spacing and array periodicity. These results demonstrate that engineered density gradients provide an effective route to deterministic control of DW propagation, with potential applications in spintronic and neuromorphic devices.

title: Metric random tilings: exact entropy and the diffraction of counted disorder
summary: Tiling mathematics has twice become the language of a state of matter: crystals, then quasicrystals, whose thermodynamics are described by the random tiling of fixed shapes. There the counted variable is the arrangement rather than the geometry, although the metric is what chemical design sets and diffraction measures. Here we introduce metric random tilings, periodic networks of locked topology whose edge lengths fluctuate under exact face closure, so that the geometry itself is countable. Purpose-built counting engines enumerate Kepler's eleven uniform networks and divide them into seven zero-entropy ones and four carriers with positive metric entropy, each certified by an explicit construction. On the honeycomb, the densest carrier, all edge-length value domains considered carry extensive entropy, with the arithmetic class reaching $s = 0.544\,k_B$ per tile (fit band 0.53--0.58), the other two $\approx 0.2$. In diffraction, translational increase of the value domain leaves the entropy exactly invariant while the coherent fraction of the Bragg intensity at fixed patch size varies from $9\times10^{-4}$ to 0.58, following the Debye--Waller law of the amplitude flow. Metric disorder thus enters the exact-counting paradigm, and is identifiable in real materials by Bragg spots wrapped in metric halos.

title: Using an energy pixels approach to estimate the size a 2nd Generation DEL must be to train a high-resolution binding model
summary: DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) are commonly used to find small-molecule binders to a target protein. But the hard part is no longer finding a hit. It is building a machine-learning model good enough to guide the medicinal chemistry that follows, one that can resolve the shift in affinity when a chemist changes a single atom. Such a model needs two things from its training data: dense sampling of the small patch of chemical space around the hit, and an adequate number of genuinely tight binders within it. A diverse naive DEL gives neither. It samples an enormous space, so any one neighborhood is covered far too thinly, and the tightest binders are rare. A model trained on that naive DEL data must extrapolate to binders tighter than any it has seen, and that is where models can fail. One way to get training data with both properties is a second-generation DEL built around the hit. We ask how complex that library must be. We treat binding as a sum of small, independent interactions, called pixels on the target and antipixels on the ligand. From the spread of affinities measured in the naive library, with no structural information and nothing yet synthesized, we estimate the complexity such a library must have to supply that dense sampling and those tight binders. The method does two useful things. It turns the number of tight binders a model needs into the number of compounds a library must contain. And it estimates the expected yield of a randomly designed second-generation DEL, so the gain from designing the library with machine learning or active learning can be measured against a baseline, without the expense of a control library as large as the experiment itself.

title: AI for Biologists: The Knowledge Boundaries of Foundation Models in the Age of Agentic Systems
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how biological research is done. Biological foundation models trained on millions of nucleotides, protein, and single-cell measurements predict protein structures, mutation effects, and cellular responses to genetic perturbations. Agentic systems, AI assistants built on large language models, can run multistep analyses from plain-language requests and increasingly call foundation models as tools. Yet it is often unclear when these models' outputs can be trusted. We frame this as a model's knowledge boundary: the range of inputs, tasks, and conditions over which its outputs are reliable. This review explains how foundation models are built and proposes that five design elements (data, architecture, training scheme, evaluation scheme, and post-analysis) define this boundary. We examine evidence on where current models succeed or fail and present standardized descriptions of model limits so that researchers, and the agents acting for them, can use these tools reliably.

title: CupOFMoCA: Coupled Objective-Guided Discrete Flows for Molecular Conjugate Assembly
summary: Molecular conjugates, including PROTACs and peptide-drug conjugates (PDCs), derive their function from the joint behavior of multiple coupled components, yet most generative approaches design these components independently and combine them only after generation. Such staged pipelines ignore cross-component dependencies and often produce conjugates that are chemically invalid, fall outside empirical conjugate distributions, or lose function upon assembly. In this work, we introduce Coupled Objective-Guided Discrete Flows for Molecular Conjugate Assembly (CupOFMoCA), a discrete generative method that enforces cross-component chemical constraints during conjugate generation. CupOFMoCA restricts guided updates to chemically feasible conjugate states and reweights local transitions using molecular design objectives. Across three PDC systems, coupled generation achieved 100% conjugation validity among valid peptides and increased valid yield over matched post-hoc filtering, with comparable predicted binding scores across the full valid sets. In three-seed evaluations of three PROTAC systems, CupOFMoCA achieved the highest assembly validity on two systems and generated more assembly-valid molecules per second than the evaluated baselines. We further evaluated the generated PROTACs with post-hoc DegradeMaster scoring and explicit-solvent molecular dynamics, supporting their predicted activity and conformational properties. Together, these results establish CupOFMoCA as an efficient generator of molecular conjugates, supporting therapeutic development via coordinated control of assembly and molecular properties.

title: Silscore: modelling siRNA potency with positional thermodynamics and data-selected nucleotide-identity terms
summary: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) enable programmable gene silencing, but candidates targeting the same transcript can differ markedly in potency. Existing predictors range from interpretable empirical rules with limited accuracy to high-capacity models that can lose performance when datasets or targets change. We present Silscore, a guide-only model that combines a quadratic preference for overall duplex stability, a position-resolved profile of nearest-neighbour stacking energies and sparse nucleotide-identity terms selected from residuals left unexplained by thermodynamics. Its main fit uses 26 parameters, fewer than half as many as any trainable comparator evaluated here. We evaluate Silscore on the canonical split of the Huesken dataset, two external datasets (Mixset and Katoh-Suzuki), and an evaluation in which the same guides are tested after training on dissimilar targets. Silscore attains the highest observed Pearson correlation in all three transfer evaluations, and the data support an advantage over every applicable comparator on Katoh-Suzuki. For a fixed evaluation set, we compare two equally sized training sets with higher or lower sequence similarity to the evaluation sequences. After training on the less similar sequences, Silscore has the highest observed correlation, and the data do not establish a change in its performance. The fitted parameters can also be interpreted directly: identity terms locate sequence effects that base-pairing energies cannot express, global stability has a data-estimated intermediate optimum, and local energy profiles recover terminal asymmetry and a preference for weaker seed and stronger central pairing. Silscore thus provides a compact, data-driven model that combines strong predictive performance with robustness when tested in new settings and expresses previously reported empirical preferences as quantities estimated from data.

title: Expanding the Decision Space of Pretrained Models through Structured Re-Decoding
summary: Native decoders limit how pretrained models combine local predictions under new structural constraints. We introduce Structured Re-Decoding (SRD), a training-free framework that constructs local candidates from model scores, samples, or external specifications, jointly optimizes their selection, and verifies reconstructed outputs. We show that candidate recombination expands feasible support and can improve attainable reward under a fixed KL divergence budget. Across molecular generation, protein design, RNA structure prediction, and antibody modeling, SRD enables improved structured inference, including verified molecules absent from the original sample pool. External chemical templates further extend SRD to noncanonical amino acids, peptide cyclization, and grammar-guided molecular construction. Preliminary experiments on a physical coherent Ising machine demonstrate the feasibility of hardware-based optimization, suggesting broader opportunities for quantum and quantum-inspired approaches to structured inference and combinatorial optimization across scientific domains.

title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
summary: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. This demonstrates that loss-based scaling laws alone are insufficient to predict when zero-shot emergent capabilities become available. The capabilities reported here emerge after training at a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio to accommodate the sparsity of paired biological interaction data. The same frozen representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods. In prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets spanning seven protein families, Bonbon achieves a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, yielding structurally novel molecules not previously reported to inhibit these proteins, including for out-of-distribution targets.

title: ANTIOCH-VS: From Sequence to Hits with Modular, Open-Source Ensemble Virtual Screening
summary: Structure-based virtual screening needs a receptor conformation that fits the ligand class, but for most targets no ligand-bound crystal is available -- and a single predicted model or an apo structure often misses the binding-competent state. We present ANTIOCH-VS, an open-source framework that runs an entire in silico screening campaign, from a protein sequence to a ranked shortlist of candidate binders, as one plug-and-play workflow. It first builds a conformational ensemble by reduced-MSA subsampling with ColabFold, then uses AlphaFold2-RAVE (AF2RAVE) -- short molecular-dynamics simulations with State Predictive Information Bottleneck analysis -- to pick out docking-ready, Boltzmann-weighted metastable states. It then detects the binding pocket, prepares receptors and ligands, docks the library across the ensemble with DOCK6 or AutoDock Vina, builds a consensus ranking, and triages the top hits by physics-based metadynamics (CTMD). We benchmark it on two very different targets, JAK2 kinase and ADRB2 GPCR, using their DUD-E benchmark sets of known binders and property-matched decoys. Starting from sequence alone -- no ligand-bound crystal, no manual intervention -- the AF2RAVE ensembles gave top-20 shortlists strongly enriched for true binders: a 20% hit rate for JAK2 and 60% for ADRB2 (random ~1-2%), on par with ligand-bound crystals and, for the kinase, above single AF2 models and an apo crystal. The full pipeline runs end to end on a workstation or HPC from a single command, or each module can be run on its own with user-supplied inputs. ANTIOCH-VS is freely available at https://github.com/tiwarylab/antioch-vs

title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
summary: Protein engineering requires navigating rugged fitness landscapes, where small sequence changes can produce large functional differences, but experimental screening can only sample a small fraction of sequence space. Thus, a central challenge is to efficiently traverse the large combinatorial space of mutations in silico. We introduce ProTEUS, a mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution. Pretrained on deep mutational scanning assays, ProTEUS learns a joint representation of sequence, evolutionary, and structural information using MutationFormer, a mutation-biased attention architecture. Variants are represented as states in this joint latent space, and mutations define actions whose functional consequences are predicted. To support exploration of many mutants, we developed a fast, physics-constrained all-atom predictor that utilizes explicit geometric constraint enforcement to achieve >10 fold increase in speed than AlphaFold3 with guaranteed physical validity. Lastly, ProTEUS refines its prediction and understanding of protein activity through closed loop experimental feedback to guide evolution toward a desired phenotype. ProTEUS surpasses established models in both zero-shot and supervised fine-tuning mutation prediction tasks. We experimentally demonstrate its utility in two closed-loop multi-objective engineering campaigns on aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase, yielding variants with >10 fold higher activity than wild type. ProTEUS provides a world-model framework that connects virtual evaluation of mutational outcomes with experimental learning for efficient protein evolution.

title: HyPLM Technical Report
summary: Protein language models (PLMs) are standard tools for variant-effect prediction, protein annotation and design, but the compute needed to train and serve them keeps growing. We present HyPLM-Flash, an efficient and open PLM trained by Hyra 2.0, the research agent developed by our team. HyPLM-Flash is a 650-million-parameter masked language model trained on 726 billion tokens, 0.73 times the data of ESM-2 650M and a fifth to an eighth of the data of E1-600M and ESM C 600M. It runs on an inference engine with fused kernels and INT8 matrix multiplication, embedding about 130,000 residues per second on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU, 1.9 to 2.7 times faster than other 600M-class encoders. In a matched evaluation against 28 public checkpoints on 32 tasks, HyPLM-Flash reaches a ProteinGym zero-shot Spearman correlation of 0.409, statistically tied with ESM-2 650M, ESM C 600M and E1-600M, and the highest organismal-fitness score among self-supervised single-sequence models. It gives the best long-range contact precision of all models evaluated, including ESM-2 15B and ESM C 6B, and a lower masked-residue loss than ESM-2 650M, ESM C 600M and E1-600M on held-out sequences and on recently released PDB chains. Matching state-of-the-art accuracy at a fraction of the training and inference cost, HyPLM-Flash sets a new Pareto frontier for protein language models. We have released the model weights and the inference engine at https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/hyra-results/tree/main.

title: HyInv Technical Report
summary: Inverse folding designs amino-acid sequences for a given protein backbone, and screening needs many candidates that are both diverse and well folded. We present HyInv, a 1.96-million-parameter backbone-conditioned graph network with an encoder-decoder architecture, trained by Hyra 2.0, the research agent developed by our team: pretrained with random-order autoregressive sequence modeling, followed by structure-reward reinforcement learning. At inference, a grouped draft-and-rewrite sampler that uses separate draft and rewrite temperatures improves refolding TM-score at matched diversity. An optimized implementation with BF16 numerics designs 128 sequences for a 402-residue backbone in 50.6 ms on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU, about 52 times faster than the reference sampler, and an exact FP32 path that returns the reference sequences is 8.7 times faster. Across five benchmark datasets and seven dataset-predictor combinations, HyInv reaches a higher average scTM than all ten external baselines at comparable or higher sequence diversity, with large margins over ProteinMPNN and ProteinZero V2. The same default setting supports de novo backbones, pocket-constrained libraries, enzyme redesign with the catalytic site kept, and loop redesign. We have released our code and model at https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/Hyra-results/tree/main/AI4Science/hyinv.

title: Yelp AI 助手融合原生 UI 与服务端驱动 UI
summary:
Yelp 为其 AI 助手采用了混合用户界面架构，将原生移动控件与服务器驱动的对话渲染相结合，实现跨平台界面的快速迭代。该方案基于 Yelp 的 CHAOS 框架（全称 Content Hosting Architecture with Optimization Strategies，带优化策略的内容托管架构）渲染对话内容，导航栏与消息输入框则保留原生实现。
Yelp 助手于 2024 年在 iOS 上推出，帮助用户向本地服务从业者提交服务需求。此后，它逐步扩展至查询商户相关信息，并可完成预订、预约、点餐等操作。
CHAOS 支持 Web、iOS 和 Android。在服务器驱动 UI 架构中，由后端定义客户端显示的内容以及如何响应交互，因此无需发布新的移动应用版本即可让界面变更触达用户。
Yelp 服务技术负责人 Daniel Andrade Groppe 强调：
我们现有的 CHAOS 框架缺少助手所需的一些能力，包括文本输入字段和网络请求。扩展框架会延迟交付，因此我们采用了混合方法：保持导航和消息输入为原生实现，同时使用 CHAOS 渲染对话区域。
这套实现将视图配置和对话数据分离。聊天会话启动时，客户端拉取 CHAOS 配置并初始化消息事件数据集。后续消息事件直接更新现有视图，无需重新拉取配置。事件类型包含持久化的用户消息和机器人消息、临时输入指示器和快速回复，以及打开目标页面的链接。后端还可以发送指令来控制界面。例如，当项目请求完成时，它可以返回一条消息、一个查看匹配的链接，以及一个禁用聊天输入的动作。这种事件驱动设计将渲染与对话逻辑分离开。
Airbnb 通过其 Ghost Platform 公开过类似的思路，该平台在 Web 和移动客户端上使用服务器定义的 UI。这两种方案都允许团队更新界面展示效果时不必每次改动都打包发布新版本客户端。Yelp 将该模型应用于对话界面，同时保留原生控件，在客户端维护消息状态与交互处理。
客户端显示已提交的消息和输入指示器，禁用输入，并向后端发送请求。收到响应后，显示回复和快速回复，并重新启用输入。恢复错误会自动重试，不可恢复的故障则禁用输入并提示用户稍后重试。
Yelp 工程师指出，该架构也带来协同复杂度，工程师需要时间来同时理解助手和 CHAOS，而且同一套逻辑在不同平台上仍可能表现不一样。将视图配置与对话数据分离实现了独立的功能开发。该架构还支持复用 Android 助手来启动 Biz Ask Anything 试点项目。Yelp 表示，这项工作为其下一代助手奠定了基础，新版助手现在可以将商家信息与用户可执行的操作连接起来。

title: 闭环 AI 自我进化：从 Skill、Harness 到模型训练与评估｜AICon北京
summary:
当 Agent 真正进入企业流程，哪些工作可以交给 AI ？50 + 实战案例揭晓答案！
AI 正在从回答问题的辅助工具，走向理解目标、调用系统、完成任务的工作承担者。当 Agent 真正进入企业流程，问题不再是 “如何把 AI 做出来”，而是哪些工作可以交给 AI、结果如何验收、权限、成本与风险如何收住。随着大模型向推理、工具调用、多模态和长任务延伸，开发重心正从单次调用转向上下文、工具、执行环境与反馈回路的设计，Coding Agent 也从代码补全演进为能理解代码库、运行测试、完成复杂任务的工程协作者。OpenAI、Google Cloud、Anthropic 的最新实践共同指向一个结论：模型决定 Agent 能做什么，工程决定它能否真正进入生产、创造价值。
在这一背景下，2026 年 AICon 人工智能开发与应用大会 · 北京站将于 12 月 18–19 日，在北京新云南皇冠假日酒店举办。本届大会以探索 A 应用边界为主题，设置 13 大技术专题，覆盖大模型后训练、推理优化、Agent 工程、知识工程、智能体评测与安全、自进化系统、AI 软件交付、原生架构及组织变革等核心方向，汇聚一线技术专家，深入分享 AI 技术突破与企业规模化落地的真实实践。
微软亚洲研究院高级研究员杨一帆已确认出席 “Self-Evolving Agents｜从经验学习到可控进化” 专题，并发表题为《闭环 AI 自我进化：从 Skill、Harness 到模型训练与评估》的主题分享。杨一帆的本次分享结合了一系列研究工作，探讨递归自我改进（RSI）的关键问题与解决方案。在技能与执行层面，SkillOpt 依据执行反馈更新可复用技能，HarnessOpt 协调工作流、工具、记忆与恢复机制的改动；在训练与评估层面，EnvOpt 随学习者的变化调整可执行训练环境，支持模型迭代训练，EvalOpt 则基于人类偏好改进评估与反馈策略，以更好地支持开放式任。RetriEvolver 展示了自我演进在异构检索系统中的应用成效。本次分享还将结合实验结果与失败案例，讨论如何明确改进对象、以证据指导改动并验证效果，据此保留有效改进、积累经验。
杨一帆，微软亚洲研究院高级研究员，主要研究智能体系统、AI 自进化以及大模型后训练相关技术。发表学术论文四十余篇，拥有十余项国际专利，获 AAAI 2026 杰出论文奖、WAIC 2026 青年优秀论文提名奖。长期担任 NeurIPS、ICLR、ICML 和 AAAI 等国际会议的领域主席。长期支持微软内部的模型研发以及产品技术转化，相关技术应用于 Office、Azure 等微软核心产品。主导的开源项目累计获得超过 2 万 GitHub Stars。
他在本次会议的详细演讲内容如下：
演讲提纲
- 递归自我改进：从执行经验到能力提升
- 改进对象：技能、执行系统、训练环境与评估机制各自解决什么问题
- 闭环设计：从任务反馈中提出改进、验证效果并积累经验
- 设计取舍：选择优化切入点，兼顾改进效果、优化成本与稳定性
- Skill 与 Harness：技能与执行系统的自我改进
- SkillOpt：依据执行反馈优化可复用技能
- HarnessOpt：协同改进工作流、工具、记忆与恢复机制
- RetriEvolver：HarnessOpt 在异构检索系统中的应用实践
- 模型训练与评估：优化学习过程本身
- EnvOpt：随学习者能力变化调整可执行训练环境，支持模型迭代训练
- EvalOpt：基于人类偏好改进评估与反馈策略，支持开放式任务
- 总结与展望
听众收益
- 理解 Skill、Harness、模型训练与评估层面的自我改进方法及其适用范围
- 获得从任务反馈到效果验证的闭环设计思路，判断哪些改动值得保留和复用
- 结合自身系统识别优化切入点，规划可逐步实施、可验证的演进路径
除此之外，本次大会还策划了Post-Training Engineering｜数据、奖励与模型能力塑造、大模型推理与算力调度实践、Knowledge Engineering｜让 Agent 理解企业、Multi-Agent Systems、智能体评测与生产可靠性探索、Agent Security｜身份、权限与行动安全、AgentOps｜企业 Agent 全生命周期管理、Self-Evolving Agents｜从经验学习到可控进化、Agentic Software Engineering｜从代码生成到软件交付、Personal Agent、AI 原生架构的演进与治理、AI 时代的组织重构、AI × Industries ｜产业智能化等 13 个专题论坛，届时将有来自不同行业、不同领域、不同企业的资深专家在现场带来前沿技术洞察和一线实践经验。

微软亚洲研究院高级研究员杨一帆已确认出席 “Self-Evolving Agents｜从经验学习到可控进化” 专题，并发表题为《闭环 AI 自我进化：从 Skill、Harness 到模型训练与评估》的主题分享。杨一帆的本次分享结合了一系列研究工作，探讨递归自我改进（RSI）的关键问题与解决方案。在技能与执行层面，SkillOpt 依据执行反馈更新可复用技能，HarnessOpt 协调工作流、工具、记忆与恢复机制的改动；在训练与评估层面，EnvOpt 随学习者的变化调整可执行训练环境，支持模型迭代训练，EvalOpt 则基于人类偏好改进评估与反馈策略，以更好地支持开放式任。RetriEvolver 展示了自我演进在异构检索系统中的应用成效。本次分享还将结合实验结果与失败案例，讨论如何明确改进对象、以证据指导改动并验证效果，据此保留有效改进、积累经验。
杨一帆，微软亚洲研究院高级研究员，主要研究智能体系统、AI 自进化以及大模型后训练相关技术。发表学术论文四十余篇，拥有十余项国际专利，获 AAAI 2026 杰出论文奖、WAIC 2026 青年优秀论文提名奖。长期担任 NeurIPS、ICLR、ICML 和 AAAI 等国际会议的领域主席。长期支持微软内部的模型研发以及产品技术转化，相关技术应用于 Office、Azure 等微软核心产品。主导的开源项目累计获得超过 2 万 GitHub Stars。
他在本次会议的详细演讲内容如下：
演讲提纲
- 递归自我改进：从执行经验到能力提升
- 改进对象：技能、执行系统、训练环境与评估机制各自解决什么问题
- 闭环设计：从任务反馈中提出改进、验证效果并积累经验
- 设计取舍：选择优化切入点，兼顾改进效果、优化成本与稳定性
- Skill 与 Harness：技能与执行系统的自我改进
- SkillOpt：依据执行反馈优化可复用技能
- HarnessOpt：协同改进工作流、工具、记忆与恢复机制
- RetriEvolver：HarnessOpt 在异构检索系统中的应用实践
- 模型训练与评估：优化学习过程本身
- EnvOpt：随学习者能力变化调整可执行训练环境，支持模型迭代训练
- EvalOpt：基于人类偏好改进评估与反馈策略，支持开放式任务
- 总结与展望
听众收益
- 理解 Skill、Harness、模型训练与评估层面的自我改进方法及其适用范围
- 获得从任务反馈到效果验证的闭环设计思路，判断哪些改动值得保留和复用
- 结合自身系统识别优化切入点，规划可逐步实施、可验证的演进路径
除此之外，本次大会还策划了Post-Training Engineering｜数据、奖励与模型能力塑造、大模型推理与算力调度实践、Knowledge Engineering｜让 Agent 理解企业、Multi-Agent Systems、智能体评测与生产可靠性探索、Agent Security｜身份、权限与行动安全、AgentOps｜企业 Agent 全生命周期管理、Self-Evolving Agents｜从经验学习到可控进化、Agentic Software Engineering｜从代码生成到软件交付、Personal Agent、AI 原生架构的演进与治理、AI 时代的组织重构、AI × Industries ｜产业智能化等 13 个专题论坛，届时将有来自不同行业、不同领域、不同企业的资深专家在现场带来前沿技术洞察和一线实践经验。

title: GitLab 19.5 发布，将智能体开发纳入可治理的 DevOps 平台能力
summary:
GitLab 19.5 于 10 月 15 日发布，将智能体软件开发和治理作为平台核心：GitLab MCP 服务器正式可用，同时扩展了外部 AI 智能体与 GitLab 交互的方式。
该版本允许 Claude Code、Cursor 等兼容 MCP 的工具访问更多 GitLab 工具目录，并调用 GitLab Duo Agent Platform 的智能体和工作流。与此同时，GitLab 增加了对外部智能体的治理控制，让安全团队能够了解哪些智能体正在被使用、谁在使用、针对哪些项目。
正式可用的 GitLab MCP 服务器通过 Model Context Protocol 为智能体开放 GitLab 平台能力。新增工具允许智能体发现群组、检查单个 CI/CD 构件文件，以及启动或监控 GitLab Duo 智能体和工作流。管理员还可以选择暴露哪些 MCP 工具集，从而减少不必要的工具以及它们占用的上下文。
为智能体提供所有可用工具会增加上下文消耗，也会增加模型可能执行的操作数量。工具集筛选是一种轻量化的最小权限代理设计方案。
GitLab.com 还引入了 MCP 速率限制：免费版用户每分钟 60 次请求，Premium 和 Ultimate 用户每分钟 600 次，重连与重试请求同样计入限额。
更重要的新增功能之一是将外部连接智能体纳入 GitLab 的 AI 治理范围。
此前，AI 治理仪表盘主要关注 GitLab Duo Agent Platform 的智能体。GitLab 19.5 允许通过 GitLab CLI 连接 Claude Code、Cursor 和 Codex 等工具。配置完成后，组织可以记录符合条件的智能体会话，包括用户、智能体、项目和时间信息，这些活动会与 GitLab 自身的智能体一起显示。审计事件还可以流式传输到 SIEM 系统。
这不只是提供一个 MCP 端点，而是迈出了重要一步：连通性提供能力，而治理决定了这种能力能否在组织规模下安全使用。
GitLab Duo CLI 新增了自动模式，允许智能体执行工具而无需为每个 Shell 命令、Git 操作或 MCP 调用请求批准。该功能默认关闭，可在实例、群组和项目级别进行控制，明确标记为“始终拒绝”（Always Deny）的工具仍会被阻止。
/goal 命令也正式可用。开发者只需描述一个开放式目标，GitLab Duo 就会交由受治理的流程完成代码实现与结果核验。
这些功能共同推动 GitLab 向智能体驱动开发模式演进：开发者只需要表达意图，由智能体在开发环境中自动执行多步任务。
这使得治理控制变得越来越重要：智能体的自主性越高，依赖人工批准每个单独操作就越不现实。
该版本同时正式发布 GitLab Secrets Manager。它基于 OpenBao 构建，与现有 GitLab 群组和项目权限集成，将密钥作用范围限定于需要它们的任务内，并为密钥操作生成审计事件。
GitLab 还扩展了安全配置模板能力，企业可以统一配置密钥检测（Secret Detection）、静态应用安全检测（SAST）的参数，例如排除路径、分析器镜像、全历史扫描等，不必在每个项目的 CI/CD 文件中重复配置。
这些能力加强了对智能体可能访问的代码库、凭证和流水线的控制，与智能体功能形成互补。
GitLab 的发展方向和 GitHub 策略越来越相似：把代码智能体变称软件生命周期的参与方。但 GitLab 的侧重点是将外部智能体接入自身现有的 DevSecOps 治理体系。
GitHub 的生态受益于 GitHub Copilot 和编码智能体的广泛覆盖，而 Cursor 和 Claude Code 等工具更侧重开发者的本地环境。GitLab 的 MCP 方案则试图让 DevOps 平台可被智能体访问，包括代码库、议题、流水线、构件以及 GitLab 原生智能体。
GitLab 关注的竞争焦点正在从“哪个编码助手生成的代码更好”转向“哪个平台能为自主智能体执行工程工作提供最安全、最有用的环境”。

title: GitHub Actions 锁文件功能正式可用，保障工作流依赖安全
summary:
GitHub 已于 2026 年 10 月 28 日正式推出 GitHub Actions 工作流依赖锁文件功能（正式版），该功能两周前刚进入公开预览阶段。
工作流可以保留清晰的标签和分支引用，运行器会执行 .github/workflows/actions.lock 文件中列出的代码提交，即便后续这些标签或分支引用发生变化也不会受影响。该功能支持 GitHub 企业云版、含数据驻留的企业云版、团队版以及免费版。正式版包含预览阶段的所有功能。
本次更新旨在解决 Actions 依赖解析长期存在的短板。类似 actions/checkout@v4 或是分支名这类引用可能会发生变化，这意味着如果某个 Action 被篡改，攻击者可以向流水线注入恶意代码，而无需修改使用该 Action 的代码库。团队虽然可以手动固定为完整的提交 SHA，但可读性会变差，而且无法固定传递依赖（如复合 Action 的依赖）。锁文件通过记录直接依赖和传递依赖的提交哈希同时解决了这两个问题。
相关工具通过 GitHub CLI 的 gh actions-lock 扩展提供，该扩展托管在 gh-actions-lock 代码库中，用于生成和维护锁文件。采用过程遵循一套工作流：工作流接入之后，所有依赖项都必须在锁文件中拥有对应的条目。Actions 运行时会执行记录的提交，无论标签或分支指向何处。团队可以进行逐步迁移，不必一次性转换整个组织。该扩展还提供了验证模式，可在不修改任何文件的情况下检查锁文件是否为最新状态，因此可以作为 CI 门禁，用于发现工作流文件与锁文件之间的差异。
Dependabot 集成解决了固定依赖带来的常见痛点——引用过期。当 Dependabot 为已接入工作流中的某个 Action 发起版本更新时，它会同时更新对应的锁文件条目。两项变更会出现在同一个拉取请求中，确保工作流引用与锁定的提交保持同步。GitHub 表示此功能无需额外配置即可使用。在治理方面，企业、组织和代码库管理员可以启用 “Require lockfile”（强制要求锁文件）策略，在对应范围内推动采用。
GitHub 明确说明了该机制的局限性：锁文件只能保证运行时使用你锁定的提交，但无法保证这些提交本身是安全的。公告建议在锁定依赖前对其进行审查。因此，该功能的安全价值取决于创建或更新条目时所做的审查工作。在实际使用中，Dependabot 的拉取请求成为了审查节点——如果团队对这些更新启用自动合并，恶意变更将直接写入锁文件。
本次发布之际，GitHub 正在收紧 Actions 的其他默认安全策略。11 月 2 日的更新公告提到，pull_request_target 将从 12 月 2 日起默认被阻止，同样是为了限制不受信任代码进入高权限工作流上下文。
正在评估是否采用该功能的团队可以查阅 GitHub 文档中关于工作流依赖锁文件的配置说明。推荐的思路：先接入少数高权限工作流（例如发布、部署流水线），在 CI 中加入过期校验，确认 Dependabot 的合并拉取请求符合现有审核流程后再启用企业级强制策略。
截至目前， 其他同类平台尚未宣布推出类似的原生功能。GitLab 的流水线安全指南建议用户手动将 include 和组件固定到提交 SHA，镜像也固定为摘要值。在 2026 年 3 月的供应链安全事件之后，GitLab 引入了开源流水线执行策略，但这些策略侧重于阻止已知攻击模式，而不是生成依赖清单。微软的 Azure Pipelines 零信任指南同样建议使用 SHA 固定方案，并建议限制 Marketplace 扩展的使用。
CircleCI 的 orb 使用中心化的语义化版本注册表而非提交哈希，该注册表具有不可变性。使用这些平台的团队通常会借助跨平台工具，例如使用 pinner 将标签固定到 SHA 并添加 CI 验证步骤，或依赖 ActionSieve 等扫描工具来标记未固定的引用。
这些工具可以固定流水线文件中写入的引用，但无法解析传递依赖，而这正是 GitHub 锁文件要解决的问题。与 GitHub 的这个功能一样，这些工具都无法判断被固定的依赖是否可信，因此锁定前的审查步骤仍然是真正起作用的安全控制点。

本次更新旨在解决 Actions 依赖解析长期存在的短板。类似 actions/checkout@v4 或是分支名这类引用可能会发生变化，这意味着如果某个 Action 被篡改，攻击者可以向流水线注入恶意代码，而无需修改使用该 Action 的代码库。团队虽然可以手动固定为完整的提交 SHA，但可读性会变差，而且无法固定传递依赖（如复合 Action 的依赖）。锁文件通过记录直接依赖和传递依赖的提交哈希同时解决了这两个问题。
相关工具通过 GitHub CLI 的 gh actions-lock 扩展提供，该扩展托管在 gh-actions-lock 代码库中，用于生成和维护锁文件。采用过程遵循一套工作流：工作流接入之后，所有依赖项都必须在锁文件中拥有对应的条目。Actions 运行时会执行记录的提交，无论标签或分支指向何处。团队可以进行逐步迁移，不必一次性转换整个组织。该扩展还提供了验证模式，可在不修改任何文件的情况下检查锁文件是否为最新状态，因此可以作为 CI 门禁，用于发现工作流文件与锁文件之间的差异。
Dependabot 集成解决了固定依赖带来的常见痛点——引用过期。当 Dependabot 为已接入工作流中的某个 Action 发起版本更新时，它会同时更新对应的锁文件条目。两项变更会出现在同一个拉取请求中，确保工作流引用与锁定的提交保持同步。GitHub 表示此功能无需额外配置即可使用。在治理方面，企业、组织和代码库管理员可以启用 “Require lockfile”（强制要求锁文件）策略，在对应范围内推动采用。
GitHub 明确说明了该机制的局限性：锁文件只能保证运行时使用你锁定的提交，但无法保证这些提交本身是安全的。公告建议在锁定依赖前对其进行审查。因此，该功能的安全价值取决于创建或更新条目时所做的审查工作。在实际使用中，Dependabot 的拉取请求成为了审查节点——如果团队对这些更新启用自动合并，恶意变更将直接写入锁文件。
本次发布之际，GitHub 正在收紧 Actions 的其他默认安全策略。11 月 2 日的更新公告提到，pull_request_target 将从 12 月 2 日起默认被阻止，同样是为了限制不受信任代码进入高权限工作流上下文。
正在评估是否采用该功能的团队可以查阅 GitHub 文档中关于工作流依赖锁文件的配置说明。推荐的思路：先接入少数高权限工作流（例如发布、部署流水线），在 CI 中加入过期校验，确认 Dependabot 的合并拉取请求符合现有审核流程后再启用企业级强制策略。
截至目前， 其他同类平台尚未宣布推出类似的原生功能。GitLab 的流水线安全指南建议用户手动将 include 和组件固定到提交 SHA，镜像也固定为摘要值。在 2026 年 3 月的供应链安全事件之后，GitLab 引入了开源流水线执行策略，但这些策略侧重于阻止已知攻击模式，而不是生成依赖清单。微软的 Azure Pipelines 零信任指南同样建议使用 SHA 固定方案，并建议限制 Marketplace 扩展的使用。
CircleCI 的 orb 使用中心化的语义化版本注册表而非提交哈希，该注册表具有不可变性。使用这些平台的团队通常会借助跨平台工具，例如使用 pinner 将标签固定到 SHA 并添加 CI 验证步骤，或依赖 ActionSieve 等扫描工具来标记未固定的引用。
这些工具可以固定流水线文件中写入的引用，但无法解析传递依赖，而这正是 GitHub 锁文件要解决的问题。与 GitHub 的这个功能一样，这些工具都无法判断被固定的依赖是否可信，因此锁定前的审查步骤仍然是真正起作用的安全控制点。

title: AI 自动写 PR，模型反而最简单：Inkitt 如何应对 Webhook 重复、CI 失败与合并冲突
summary:
Inkitt 构建了一个一次性拉取请求（PR）创建器，可以自动完成小型、低风险的软件变更，从接收任务一直执行到生成可供测试和审查的草稿 PR。该工作流可以通过 Slack、Linear，或者另一个智能体发起的 API 调用触发，并在远程基础设施上运行，从而减少开发者在本地配置和监督编码智能体的需要。Inkitt Tech 在一篇技术文章中表示，该系统已经每天用于交付代码。
Inkitt 首席工程师 Agi Letkiewicz Tanner 将其描述为：
一种事件驱动的编排器，它负责协调短生命周期的智能体容器，而不是依赖固定流水线。
各个阶段分别负责需求说明、实现、验证、CI 失败修复和合并冲突解决。编排器会将每次运行的状态持久化到数据库中，因此执行过程可以从已经记录的状态继续恢复。
Inkitt 一次性 PR 创建器架构（来源：Inkitt 博客文章）
该编排器将决策逻辑与副作用分离。其核心状态转换函数会根据当前运行状态和传入事件确定下一步操作，但不会直接访问数据库、网络或语言模型。编排器负责保管外部系统的凭证，智能体容器则只会获得短期有效的代码仓库 Token 和模型凭证。智能体无法直接访问 Slack 或 Linear 凭证、云身份，也不能随意建立网络连接。另有一项独立检查会查看实际的 Git Diff，确保变更没有触及受限制的路径。
Inkitt 将自动化限制在预先定义的边界内。涉及数据库迁移、Schema 或共享契约变更、CI 和容器构建配置、身份验证、支付代码，以及软件包添加或更新的任务都会被拒绝。验证、CI 修复和合并冲突解决最多分别尝试两次。对于重复投递的 Webhook，系统会通过去重和条件数据库写入进行处理，将幂等操作原则应用到可能重试或接收重复事件的工作流中。在判断 CI 是否完成时，编排器会查询 GitHub，确认所有相关任务都已经结束，而不会把每一个任务事件都当作整个工作流完成的信号。
Tanner 在介绍幂等性、锁、重试预算和权限等实现难题时写道：
模型反而是最简单的部分。
该设计与其他编码智能体采用了一些相同的防护措施，但使用了不同的编排模型。GitHub Copilot 的云端智能体同样会限制智能体权限，并要求在合并前进行人工审查；SWE-agent则专注于通过模型驱动的界面浏览、编辑和执行代码，从而解决代码仓库中的问题。Inkitt 的方案更强调持久化工作流状态、有限重试，以及对外部操作的集中控制。
人工审批仍然是 Inkitt 流程的一部分。系统会创建草稿 PR，无法绕过分支保护，也不能自行合并变更。当 CI 通过并且变更进入预发布环境时，系统会通知任务发起者。之后必须由人工将 PR 标记为可供审查，并管理审查者请求和审批。对于规模更大的任务，Inkitt 还维护了一个本地版本，让人工持续参与开发过程。

title: 从提效到扩能：AI 驱动小团队的能力突破与组织演进｜AICon北京
summary:
当 Agent 真正进入企业流程，哪些工作可以交给 AI ？50 + 实战案例揭晓答案！
AI 正在从回答问题的辅助工具，走向理解目标、调用系统、完成任务的工作承担者。当 Agent 真正进入企业流程，问题不再是 “如何把 AI 做出来”，而是哪些工作可以交给 AI、结果如何验收、权限、成本与风险如何收住。随着大模型向推理、工具调用、多模态和长任务延伸，开发重心正从单次调用转向上下文、工具、执行环境与反馈回路的设计，Coding Agent 也从代码补全演进为能理解代码库、运行测试、完成复杂任务的工程协作者。OpenAI、Google Cloud、Anthropic 的最新实践共同指向一个结论：模型决定 Agent 能做什么，工程决定它能否真正进入生产、创造价值。
在这一背景下，2026 年 AICon 人工智能开发与应用大会 · 北京站正式启动。本次大会将于 12 月 18–19 日，在北京新云南皇冠假日酒店举办。本届大会以探索 A 应用边界为主题，设置 13 大技术专题，覆盖大模型后训练、推理优化、Agent 工程、知识工程、智能体评测与安全、自进化系统、AI 软件交付、原生架构及组织变革等核心方向，汇聚一线技术专家，深入分享 AI 技术突破与企业规模化落地的真实实践。
彩讯股份 Nexus Lab 研发负责人高梓耕已确认出席 “Multi-Agent Systems” 专题，并发表题为《从计划到交付：Nexus WorkGraph 的多 Agent 长程执行实践》的主题分享。在早期的多智能体探索中，高梓耕团队先通过提示词与程序编排串联任务规划、Agent 选择和执行，随后通过工具调用建立主智能体向子智能体委派任务的机制。随着协作从局部子任务扩展到多个独立智能体持续参与的工作，高梓耕团队发现，除任务委派和消息交流之外，仍需解决信息如何共享、责任如何交接、结果如何验收，以及计划变化或执行中断后如何继续等问题。高梓耕的本次分享将从这些实践问题出发，重点介绍 Nexus 中 Room 与 WorkGraph 的设计与实现。Room 通过公私域通信、按成员组织的上下文与定向调度，处理信息共享和成员之间的协作交接；WorkGraph 将任务、依赖、责任、提交与验收组织为持久化的工作图，并关联实际运行记录。围绕消息投递、任务分派、提交验收与异常恢复等关键链路，说明如何通过持久队列、计划版本管理、验收约束和未知结果对账，应对长程协作中的任务推进与动态调整，并进一步介绍如何从具体执行中提取可复用的协作结构。
高梓耕，彩讯 Nexus Lab 研发负责人。长期从事企业级大模型应用与智能体系统的研究与实践，专注 RAG、上下文工程、多智能体协作与可信 AI。参与 AIBOX 2.0 智能体开发平台建设，推动大模型能力在知识问答、深度研究、数据分析等企业场景中的落地。近期主导开发开源项目 Nexus，致力于探索多人、多智能体共同参与复杂任务的 Room 式人机协同模式，推动 AI 从单一对话工具走向可持续参与企业工作的协作空间。他在本次会议的详细演讲内容如下：
他在本次会议的详细演讲内容如下：
演讲提纲
1. 三阶段探索：从工程流程到工具委派，再到持续协作
- 第一阶段：由程序连接多个处理阶段。回顾提示词编排中的路由偏差、阶段信息损失与异常处理成本
- 第二阶段：由模型通过工具协议表达下一步行动。说明主智能体如何通过工具调用委派子任务，以及宿主如何管理独立执行与结果回收
- 第三阶段：多个持续存在的 Agent 共同工作。分析持续协作中的公私通信、成员唤醒与责任交接需求，引出 Room 与 WorkGraph
2. Room：先建立成员之间的通信与调度机制
- 从共享对话到独立执行。介绍共享会话与成员独立运行的组织方式，以及公区事实、工具过程和私域历史的边界
- 从公开发言到定向交接。说明公开回复中的 `@` 如何触发交接，以及忙碌排队、投递去重与回复归属的处理
- 从私聊到可配置的回复路线。介绍收件人、唤醒对象与回复去向的独立配置，明确消息可见性与行动范围
- 从全量历史到按成员组织上下文。说明增量消息、消费游标与默认路由如何配合，为成员提供本轮所需信息
- Room 之后仍然缺什么。分析消息记录在任务分派、依赖判断和结果验收上的局限，引出 WorkGraph
3. WorkGraph：从记录执行过程，到保存责任与验收
- 先记录运行，再识别日志的边界。区分运行成功与业务完成，说明日志为何不足以确定责任和验收结论
- 从线性步骤转向显式依赖。介绍工作项、依赖与分派如何组织并行协作，并支持责任交接和换人接管
- 把“做了”“提交了”“验收了”分开。拆解执行尝试、提交与验收的关系，说明被接受的交付如何满足下游硬依赖
- 把运行证据关联回责任。介绍责任图与运行图的关联方式，以及模型如何按角色权限查询状态与证据
- 任务结构错误时，调整计划而不是覆盖历史。说明计划版本管理，以及重试、返工、接管和结果未知时的对账处理
4. 协作方法复用：从每次重新规划，到可迭代的结构
- 为什么完成一次还不够。讨论重复规划的成本，以及我们早期固定脚本在结构调整上的局限
- 选择复用责任结构。介绍如何从已完成执行中提取职责、依赖与验收要求，形成方法草图
- 让结构能够修改，但修改有边界。说明草图的版本化编辑、校验与保存，以及如何结合 Skill 生成新任务的执行计划
- 复用不能替代本次判断。讨论复用中的动态适配边界，以及质量、延迟和总成本的验证方法
5. 实践总结与仍在思考的问题
- 总结协作机制的分工。归纳 Room 的通信与调度、WorkGraph 的责任与验收如何配合，形成从任务分派到交付确认的完整过程
- 讨论实践中的验证与取舍。说明长程任务的完成质量、恢复能力和运行成本如何评估，以及动态调整与人工介入之间的边界
- 提出面向多人多智能体的开放问题。讨论多方目标与权限如何协调、责任如何交接，以及 WorkGraph 能否进一步表达持续的协作关系
听众受益
- 理解多智能体架构的形成过程：从路由、工具循环、子任务委派到持续协作，辨别不同机制的适用条件及新增工程成本
- 获得可落地的机制参考：了解公私上下文、持久交接、责任与尝试分离、提交验收、计划版本和未知结果对账如何配合
- 掌握复用与验证的切入点：理解如何从具体执行抽取协作结构、适配新任务，并从交付质量、恢复情况和总成本验证其效果

content_preview:
当 Agent 真正进入企业流程，哪些工作可以交给 AI ？50 + 实战案例揭晓答案！
AI 正在从回答问题的辅助工具，走向理解目标、调用系统、完成任务的工作承担者。当 Agent 真正进入企业流程，问题不再是 “如何把 AI 做出来”，而是哪些工作可以交给 AI、结果如何验收、权限、成本与风险如何收住。随着大模型向推理、工具调用、多模态和长任务延伸，开发重心正从单次调用转向上下文、工具、执行环境与反馈回路的设计，Coding Agent 也从代码补全演进为能理解代码库、运行测试、完成复杂任务的工程协作者。OpenAI、Google Cloud、Anthropic 的最新实践共同指向一个结论：模型决定 Agent 能做什么，工程决定它能否真正进入生产、创造价值。
在这一背景下，2026 年 AICon 人工智能开发与应用大会 · 北京站正式启动。本次大会将于 12 月 18–19 日，在北京新云南皇冠假日酒店举办。本届大会以探索 A 应用边界为主题，设置 13 大技术专题，覆盖大模型后训练、推理优化、Agent 工程、知识工程、智能体评测与安全、自进化系统、AI 软件交付、原生架构及组织变革等核心方向，汇聚一线技术专家，深入分享 AI 技术突破与企业规模化落地的真实实践。
彩讯股份 Nexus Lab 研发负责人高梓耕已确认出席 “Multi-Agent Systems” 专题，并发表题为《从计划到交付：Nexus WorkGraph 的多 Agent 长程执行实践》的主题分享。在早期的多智能体探索中，高梓耕团队先通过提示词与程序编排串联任务规划、Agent 选择和执行，随后通过工具调用建立主智能体向子智能体委派任务的机制。随着协作从局部子任务扩展到多个独立智能体持续参与的工作，高梓耕团队发现，除任务委派和消息交流之外，仍需解决信息如何共享、责任如何交接、结果如何验收，以及计划变化或执行中断后如何继续等问题。高梓耕的本次分享将从这些实践问题出发，重点介绍 Nexus 中 Room 与 WorkGraph 的设计与实现。Room 通过公私域通信、按成员组织的上下文与定向调度，处理信息共享和成员之间的协作交接；WorkGraph 将任务、依赖、责任、提交与验收组织为持久化的工作图，并关联实际运行记录。围绕消息投递、任务分派、提交验收与异常恢复等关键链路，说明如何通过持久队列、计划版本管理、验收约束和未知结果对账，应对长程协作中的任务推进与动态调整，并进一步介绍如何从具体执行中提取可复用的协作结构。
高梓耕，彩讯 Nexus Lab 研发负责人。长期从事企业级大模型应用与智能体系统的研究与实践，专注 RAG、上下文工程、多智能体协作与可信 AI。参与 AIBOX 2.0 智能体开发平台建设，推动大模型能力在知识问答、深度研究、数据分析等企业场景中的落地。近期主导开发开源项目 Nexus，致力于探索多人、多智能体共同参与复杂任务的 Room 式人机协同模式，推动 AI 从单一对话工具走向可持续参与企业工作的协作空间。他在本次会议的详细演讲内容如下：
他在本次会议的详细演讲内容如下：
演讲提纲
1. 三阶段探索：从工程流程到工具委派，再到持续协作
- 第一阶段：由程序连接多个处理阶段。回顾提示词编排中的路由偏差、阶段信息损失与异常处理成本
- 第二阶段：由模型通过工具协议表达下一步行动。说明主智能体如何通过工具调用委派子任务，以及宿主如何管理独立执行与结果回收
- 第三阶段：多个持续存在的 Agent 共同工作。分析持续协作中的公私通信、成员唤醒与责任交接需求，引出 Room 与 WorkGraph
2. Room：先建立成员之间的通信与调度机制
- 从共享对话到独立执行。介绍共享会话与成员独立运行的组织方式，以及公区事实、工具过程和私域历史的边界
- 从公开发言到定向交接。说明公开回复中的 `@` 如何触发交接，以及忙碌排队、投递去重与回复归属的处理
- 从私聊到可配置的回复路线。介绍收件人、唤醒对象与回复去向的独立配置，明确消息可见性与行动范围
- 从全量历史到按成员组织上下文。说明增量消息、消费游标与默认路由如何配合，为成员提供本轮所需信息
- Room 之后仍然缺什么。分析消息记录在任务分派、依赖判断和结果验收上的局限，引出 WorkGraph
3. WorkGraph：从记录执行过程，到保存责任与验收
- 先记录运行，再识别日志的边界。区分运行成功与业务完成，说明日志为何不足以确定责任和验收结论
- 从线性步骤转向显式依赖。介绍工作项、依赖与分派如何组织并行协作，并支持责任交接和换人接管
- 把“做了”“提交了”“验收了”分开。拆解执行尝试、提交与验收的关系，说明被接受的交付如何满足下游硬依赖
- 把运行证据关联回责任。介绍责任图与运行图的关联方式，以及模型如何按角色权限查询状态与证据
- 任务结构错误时，调整计划而不是覆盖历史。说明计划版本管理，以及重试、返工、接管和结果未知时的对账处理
4. 协作方法复用：从每次重新规划，到可迭代的结构
- 为什么完成一次还不够。讨论重复规划的成本，以及我们早期固定脚本在结构调整上的局限
- 选择复用责任结构。介绍如何从已完成执行中提取职责、依赖与验收要求，形成方法草图
- 让结构能够修改，但修改有边界。说明草图的版本化编辑、校验与保存，以及如何结合 Skill 生成新任务的执行计划
- 复用不能替代本次判断。讨论复用中的动态适配边界，以及质量、延迟和总成本的验证方法
5. 实践总结与仍在思考的问题
- 总结协作机制的分工。归纳 Room 的通信与调度、WorkGraph 的责任与验收如何配合，形成从任务分派到交付确认的完整过程
- 讨论实践中的验证与取舍。说明长程任务的完成质量、恢复能力和运行成本如何评估，以及动态调整与人工介入之间的边界
- 提出面向多人多智能体的开放问题。讨论多方目标与权限如何协调、责任如何交接，以及 WorkGraph 能否进一步表达持续的协作关系
听众受益
- 理解多智能体架构的形成过程：从路由、工具循环、子任务委派到持续协作，辨别不同机制的适用条件及新增工程成本
- 获得可落地的机制参考：了解公私上下文、持久交接、责任与尝试分离、提交验收、计划版本和未知结果对账如何配合
- 掌握复用与验证的切入点：理解如何从具体执行抽取协作结构、适配新任务，并从交付质量、恢复情况和总成本验证其效果
除此之外，本次大会还策划了 Post-Training Engineering｜数据、奖励与模型能力塑造、大模型推理与算力调度实践、Knowledge Engineering｜让 Agent 理解企业、Multi-Agent Systems、智能体评测与生产可靠性探索、Agent Security｜身份、权限与行动安全、AgentOps｜企业 Agent 全生命周期管理、Self-Evolving Agents｜从经验学习到可控进化、Agentic Software Engineering｜从代码生成到软件交付、Personal Agent、AI 原生架构的演进与治理、AI 时代的组织重构、AI × Industries ｜产业智能化等 13 个专题论坛，届时将有来自不同行业、不同领域、不同企业的资深专家在现场带来前沿技术洞察和一线实践经验。
